# A loop over one slice that writes another is limited by the slice it ranges over.
# With a destination longer than the source the vector loop used to run forever: it
# was bounded by len(dst), and loading from the exhausted source returns no
# elements. A destination shorter than the source panics, as the scalar loop does.

exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
cmpenv stderr stderr.want
cmp ops_simd.go ops_simd.go.want

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

func Scale(dst, src []float32, f float32) {
	for i, v := range src {
		dst[i] = v * f
	}
}
-- ops_simd.go.want --
//go:build goexperiment.simd

package test

import "simd"

func Scale(dst, src []float32, f float32) {
	_vcFloat32s0 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(f)
	if len(src) > 0 {
		_ = dst[len(src)-1]
		_ = src[len(src)-1]
		for _i := 0; _i < len(src); {
			_v1, _n := simd.LoadFloat32sPart(src[_i:len(src)])
			_v1.Mul(_vcFloat32s0).StorePart(dst[_i:len(src)])
			_i += _n
		}
	}
}
-- stderr.want --
loopvec: rewrote 1 loop(s) in $WORK/ops.go
-- testmain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/test"
)

func try(f func()) (panicked bool) {
	defer func() { panicked = recover() != nil }()
	f()
	return
}

func main() {
	dst := make([]float32, 8)
	test.Scale(dst, []float32{1, 2, 3}, 2)
	fmt.Println(dst)
	dst = make([]float32, 3)
	test.Scale(dst, []float32{1, 2, 3}, 2)
	fmt.Println(dst)
	short := make([]float32, 3)
	fmt.Println(try(func() { test.Scale(short, []float32{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, 2) }))
	untouched := []float32{7, 7, 7, 7}
	test.Scale(untouched, nil, 2)
	fmt.Println(untouched)
}
-- testmain/output --
[2 4 6 0 0 0 0 0]
[2 4 6]
true
[7 7 7 7]
